I'm 65 years old and I've been farming these fields in Quzhou for more than 40 years. I only went to primary school, but I know this land and these crops better than any book. My wheat is already in the ground — I sowed about 30 jin of improved seed per mu last October after rotary tilling the soil. I have 7 mu planted to winter wheat, and that's the crop I'm managing right now.

Right now the wheat is greening up, and I need to topdress it with urea and compound fertilizer when the weather warms. I'll irrigate it four times total — one more winter irrigation if needed, and then three times in spring at jointing, heading, and grain-filling. I'll spray for aphids and powdery mildew about four times. I expect to harvest around 550 kg per mu in early June if the weather cooperates.

As soon as the wheat comes off, I'll plant summer maize on the same 7 mu. I buy hybrid seed every year — Denghai or something similar from the seed shop — and I plant it no-tillage, direct seeding right into the wheat stubble. I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting and side-dress with a bit more nitrogen when the plants are knee-high. Maize needs two good irrigations, one when it's shooting and another at filling. I'll spray for corn borer and weeds three times. I expect about 600 kg per mu by late September.

I don't grow cotton or vegetables like some of my neighbors. I'm getting old, and wheat-maize is what I know. The grain buyers come to the village, and I get a small government subsidy for grain. I keep some wheat for my family's flour, feed the maize to my chickens, and sell the rest. This rotation has fed my family for generations, and I see no reason to change it now.
